baseline_transport: NCCL logs show SHM/direct/direct, with shared host buffers
forced_phb_transport: NCCL_P2P_LEVEL=PHB diagnostic logs show P2P/CUMEM; slower for all tested gradient payload sizes
important_limitations: Previous 31.16% backward stage combines computation, communication, overlap and synchronization; it is not the communication fraction.
These measurements synchronize all ready synthetic gradient buckets with no backward computation; they do not measure exposed DDP communication tail.
BF16 tests measure half-size payload only, excluding casting, gradient numerical error and convergence impact.
Bucket-capacity comparisons here exclude overlap changes in a real backward pass; whole parameter tensors may make real DDP buckets differ from these synthetic slices.
The baseline correctness check covered the first element of each constant tensor; the P2P trial checked every element for the expected sum.
Microbenchmark latency is not a guaranteed bound or predicted end-to-end training speedup.
recommendations: Keep default NCCL transport; do not force P2P_LEVEL=PHB on this host based on measured regression.
BF16 gradient communication is a candidate for a short real-model A/B test with numerical checks; parameters and optimizer can remain FP32.
Retain the default 25 MiB DDP bucket size until a real backward-overlap profile shows a reason to change it; 8/25/50 MiB synthetic tests had nearly identical baseline latency.
Profile the uncovered communication tail before promising a training speedup. Prioritize frozen-vision caching over speculative large communication gains.
Do not remove global token/sample loss normalization. Its standalone scalar all-reduce latency was around 0.17 ms; the previously measured 51 ms stage includes rank imbalance and surrounding work.
Gradient accumulation can reduce synchronization frequency if increasing effective batch size, but changes optimization cadence; splitting the same global batch is not automatically faster.
